slides.title: What's next

elements.text: I2I2V2V: edit one frame, the video follows.

slides.speech: MotionV2V showed you can edit a real video without regenerating it, but only its motion. On images, any edit already works: Nano Banana takes a picture and an instruction and changes just that. Video editors exist too, like VACE and AnyV2V, but each is built for a few kinds of edit, and I'll compare against them. So the plan is I2I2V2V: you edit one frame with an image editor, and a video model carries that edit through the whole clip. Here's an early result. Driving video, plus an edited first frame, gives the edited video. Same rocket launch, new look. Tobias Gerts made this one in ComfyUI, on a video model from my internship.

slides.title: LoraPlexer: one LoRA, many modes

elements.text: 100 community LoRAs merged into one rank-32 LoRA. Same prompt, same seed.

slides.speech: One editor has to take many control signals at once, edges, depth, relighting, a style, and right now each is its own LoRA, and stacked LoRAs fight. So the second piece is LoraPlexer: many control handles in one small add-on to the same pretrained model, and you switch between them. This is a proof of concept: a hundred community LoRAs merged into one rank-32 LoRA with no training, running six different modes with the same prompt and the same seed. The next step is distilling them properly, across noise levels and with classifier-free guidance still working. [CONFIRM: the six tile labels "3D animated", "storybook", "live action", "soft 3D", "2D anime", "3D + live mix" were guessed from how each tile looks; swap in the real mode names.]

slides.title: Where the data comes from

elements.text: The image editor makes the video training data.

slides.speech: Data is the same trick as MAGICK. There I got transparency data out of a model that can't make transparency. Here, image editors can already edit many frames of a clip at once and keep them consistent, so I use them to build paired before-and-after video data. Same person, same motion, different hair, clothes, even a puppet.

slides.title: The plan

elements.text: Feb–Apr: train I2I2V2V + merge LoRAs into LoraPlexer
Apr–Jun: evaluate vs per-frame editing, VACE, AnyV2V
Summer: paper, then write thesis and defend
Measure: did it edit, did it keep the rest, does it flicker, user study.

slides.speech: Here's the plan. First couple months, data. Then train I2I2V2V on an open video model and fold the control LoRAs into one. Then evaluate against the obvious baselines: editing every frame separately with Nano Banana, which flickers, first-frame edit plus image-to-video, and VACE and AnyV2V. I'll measure three things: did it make the edit, did it leave everything else alone, and does it flicker, plus a user study like MotionV2V. Biggest risks: edits drifting over time, where my fallback is warped noise from Go-with-the-Flow, and LoRAs interfering when merged, where the fallback is keeping them separate and only sharing the base. Then paper, thesis, defense.
